title: Retune the two-stage round split and learning rate
spec: Keep the current architecture exactly (physchem ridge base, then XGBoost fitting the ridge residuals in two stages: squared-error rounds followed by absoluteerror rounds continued from the first booster). Change only the boosting budget: set learning_rate=0.02 for both stages, stage1 n_estimators=300 with objective reg:squarederror, and stage2 n_estimators=900 with objective reg:absoluteerror continued via xgb_model=stage1.get_booster(). Leave max_depth=6, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=3, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8 unchanged. The point is that the L2 warm start may need more rounds and a slower rate once the L1 phase is long; total wall time should stay well under the limit since each fit is only a few hundred shallow trees on 728 rows.

title: Pseudo-Huber loss for the second boosting stage
spec: In the current two-stage residual model, replace the stage-2 objective reg:absoluteerror with XGBoost's built-in reg:pseudohubererror and set huber_slope=0.3 (roughly a third of the target's spread, so most residuals are in the quadratic regime and only the tails are down-weighted). Keep stage 1 as 200 rounds of reg:squarederror and keep stage 2 continuing from stage 1's booster with the same 400 rounds and the same tree hyperparameters (max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=3). Everything else, including the physchem ridge base and the features, stays as is. The aim is a smoother gradient than pure L1 while still being robust, which should help MAE on a 728-row dataset where the L1 gradient is piecewise constant and uninformative.

title: Average the two-stage model over five seeds
spec: Wrap the existing XGBoost two-stage residual fit in a loop over five seeds derived deterministically from the seed argument (for example seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4, used as random_state for both stages). Keep the physchem ridge base fitted once outside the loop and keep all features and hyperparameters identical to the current script; only the XGBoost random_state changes between members. Average the five residual predictions (plain mean) and add the ridge base prediction to get the final output. Nothing else changes. With subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.3 the individual fits are noticeably stochastic, so seed averaging should remove part of the model variance; five fits of 600 total rounds on 728 rows is still fast enough for 15 folds inside ten minutes.

title: Choose the number of L1 rounds by inner scaffold-grouped CV
spec: Pick the stage-2 boosting budget per fold instead of hard-coding 400. Inside fit_predict, after computing the ridge base and the feature matrix, run a 4-fold GroupKFold over the training molecules grouped by Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, falling back to the SMILES itself if it fails). For each inner fold, fit the same two-stage model on the inner-train part and evaluate inner-validation MAE at stage-2 round counts in {100, 200, 400, 700, 1000} using the booster's iteration_range / ntree_limit so one fit covers all candidates. Average the MAE curves across the four inner folds, pick the best round count, then refit the two-stage model on the full training set with that many stage-2 rounds and predict. Keep features, ridge base and all tree hyperparameters unchanged.

title: Snapshot averaging over the tail of the L1 stage
spec: Keep the current two-stage model but, instead of using only the final booster, average predictions from several snapshots along the stage-2 L1 trajectory. After fitting stage 2 as it is now (400 rounds continued from the 200-round L2 warm start), predict the test set at cumulative round counts 300, 400, 500 and 600 by calling the booster with iteration_range=(0, k) for each k (use xgboost.DMatrix or the sklearn wrapper's iteration_range argument), with stage 2 extended to 600 rounds so all snapshots exist. Average those four prediction vectors and add the ridge base. Keep features, ridge base and all tree hyperparameters as they are. Boosted MAE models tend to oscillate late in training because the L1 gradient is a sign, so averaging nearby snapshots should cut that oscillation at essentially no extra cost.

title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour residual correction
spec: Add a small local correction on top of the current pipeline. First compute out-of-fold predictions for the training set with a 5-fold GroupKFold grouped by Murcko scaffold, using exactly the existing model (ridge base plus two-stage XGBoost), and form training residuals r_i = y_i - oof_pred_i. Then, for every test molecule, find its 5 nearest training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) and compute a similarity-weighted mean of their residuals, with weights equal to the similarity raised to the fourth power. Add 0.5 times that weighted residual mean to the model's prediction, but only when the top similarity is at least 0.5; otherwise add nothing. Keep everything else unchanged. This targets systematic local bias in regions where the global model is consistently off.

title: Similarity-gated shrinkage toward the training median
spec: Leave the model untouched and post-process the predictions. For each test molecule compute its maximum Tanimoto similarity s to any training molecule, using binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits). Map s to a trust weight w = clip((s - 0.2) / 0.3, 0, 1), so molecules with max similarity at or below 0.2 are fully distrusted and those at or above 0.5 are fully trusted. Return w * pred + (1 - w) * m, where pred is the current pipeline's prediction and m is the median of train_y. Compute the fingerprints once per molecule with the existing caching style. Because every fold tests on unseen scaffolds, some test molecules are far from the training set, and for MAE it is better to fall back toward the median than to trust a confident extrapolation.

title: Ionization and polarity descriptors in the ridge base
spec: Enrich only the linear physchem base, which currently uses TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds and the aromatic-atom fraction. Append to that vector: counts of carboxylic acid, primary/secondary/tertiary amine, sulfonamide and phenol groups via RDKit SMARTS matches; the formal-charge counts of positively and negatively charged atoms; Descriptors.NumHeteroatoms; Descriptors.FractionCSP3; Descriptors.LabuteASA; and Descriptors.MolMR. Standardize the enlarged vector with the same StandardScaler and fit the same Ridge(alpha=1.0); the XGBoost two-stage model keeps fitting the residuals of this base on the unchanged Morgan-plus-descriptor features. Ionization state is the main physical driver of passive permeability, so making it explicit and linear should give the booster cleaner residuals to learn.

title: Rank-Gaussian target transform with inverse mapping
spec: Train the whole existing pipeline on a rank-Gaussian version of the target and invert the transform at prediction time. Fit a sklearn QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=min(200, n_train), random_state=seed) on train_y reshaped to a column, transform the targets, run the current ridge base plus two-stage XGBoost residual model on the transformed targets exactly as now, then apply inverse_transform to the test predictions before returning them. Clip the transformed-space predictions to the min and max of the transformed training targets before inverting, so the inverse mapping stays inside the fitted support. Keep features and all hyperparameters unchanged. A Gaussianized target makes the squared-error warm-up stage better behaved if the raw permeability values are skewed or have heavy tails.

title: Stronger leaf and split regularization in XGBoost
spec: Keep the architecture and the two-stage schedule but regularize the trees harder, since 728 rows with roughly 2200 features is a strongly over-parameterized setting. Change the shared XGBoost parameters to max_depth=4, min_child_weight=6, reg_lambda=5.0, gamma=0.5, subsample=0.7, colsample_bytree=0.2, colsample_bylevel=0.7, learning_rate=0.03, and compensate for the shallower trees by using 300 stage-1 squared-error rounds and 700 stage-2 absoluteerror rounds continued from stage 1. The physchem ridge base, the features and the overall two-stage structure stay exactly as they are. The hypothesis is that the current depth-6 trees with min_child_weight=3 can isolate individual scaffolds, which hurts on folds that test on unseen skeletons.

title: Seed-bag the gradient boosting residual model
spec: Keep the Ridge baseline on physchem descriptors and the feature matrix exactly as they are. Change only the residual model: instead of one two-stage XGBoost fit, run the same two-stage fit (200 squared-error trees then 400 absolute-error trees continuing from the first booster) five times with random_state set to seed, seed+1, seed+2, seed+3, seed+4, and return base_te plus the arithmetic mean of the five stage-2 test predictions. This averages away variance coming from subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.3. Runtime grows roughly fivefold but should stay well inside the limit.

title: Blend a CatBoost MAE residual model with the XGBoost one
spec: Keep the existing pipeline intact (Ridge baseline, two-stage XGBoost on the residual y minus base_tr). Add a second residual learner: CatBoostRegressor on the same training matrix and the same residual target with loss_function='MAE', iterations=1500, learning_rate=0.03, depth=6, rsm=0.1, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0. Final prediction is base_te plus the equal-weight average of the XGBoost stage-2 prediction and the CatBoost prediction. Import CatBoostRegressor from catboost at the top of the file.

title: Add MACCS keys and atom-pair counts to the features
spec: Extend featurize_one so the cached vector concatenates four pieces: the current Morgan count fingerprint, the current RDKit descriptor block, the 167 MACCS keys (from rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to a float32 array), and a 1024-length atom-pair count fingerprint from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Leave fit_predict and all model hyperparameters unchanged. The aim is to supply substructure-key and topological-distance information that Morgan radius 2 does not encode.

title: Prune rare and constant feature columns inside each fit
spec: In fit_predict, after building Xtr and Xte, derive a column mask using training data only: keep a column if it is non-zero in at least five training molecules and its training variance is above zero. Apply the same mask to Xtr and Xte before fitting the boosting stages. Everything else is unchanged. With roughly 580 training rows per fold, most of the 2048 Morgan bits are near-empty, and removing them shrinks the space the column-subsampling draws from so each tree sees more informative candidate splits.

title: Replace the Ridge baseline with a cross-fitted linear baseline
spec: The current Ridge baseline is fit on the full training set and then subtracted from the same rows, so the residuals the booster learns are optimistically small and mismatched with test-time residuals. Change it to an out-of-fold baseline: use sklearn.model_selection.KFold with 10 splits shuffled by seed on the scaled physchem matrix, fill base_tr with out-of-fold Ridge predictions, and compute base_te from a Ridge refit on all training rows. The booster then trains on honest residuals. Keep alpha=1.0, the descriptor set, the feature matrix and all boosting hyperparameters as they are.

title: Tune the boosting hyperparameters toward a shallower, slower fit
spec: Keep the architecture and features exactly as they are and only change the shared params dict and the tree counts. Set max_depth to 4, learning_rate to 0.015, subsample to 0.7, colsample_bytree to 0.2, min_child_weight to 5, and add reg_lambda=2.0. Raise the stage-1 squared-error round count to 400 and the stage-2 absolute-error round count to 1200 so the total shrinkage budget is comparable. With under 600 training rows and thousands of columns, depth 6 trees at learning rate 0.03 are likely overfitting scaffold-held-out folds.

title: Average predictions over several Morgan radii
spec: Generalise featurize so it takes a radius argument and builds a separate cached feature matrix per radius, each being the Morgan count fingerprint at that radius concatenated with the usual RDKit descriptor block. In fit_predict, run the complete existing residual-boosting procedure three times, once on the radius-1 matrix, once on radius 2 and once on radius 3, and return base_te plus the mean of the three residual predictions. The shared Ridge baseline is computed once. Different radii capture different substructure scales and their errors should partially cancel.

title: Stack a fingerprint-similarity kernel ridge model into the ensemble
spec: Add a third predictor alongside the current pipeline: build binary Morgan bit vectors (radius 2, 2048 bits) for train and test, compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix between train and train and between test and train with numpy (intersection over union of the binary matrices), and fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) on the train-train similarity matrix against the raw target y. Predict on the test-train matrix. Final output is 0.7 times the current prediction plus 0.3 times this similarity-based prediction. Similarity models extrapolate differently from trees on unseen scaffolds.

title: Winsorize the target and train the booster on the clipped scale
spec: Caco-2 log-permeability values have a long low tail that an MAE objective handles but a squared-error warm-start stage does not. Before fitting, clip the training target to its 2nd and 98th training percentiles and use the clipped values everywhere the booster and the Ridge baseline are fitted. Do not clip the returned predictions. Keep the feature matrix, the two-stage structure and all hyperparameters unchanged. This limits how far a handful of extreme molecules can drag the early squared-error rounds.

title: Pick the stage-2 round count by internal scaffold-grouped validation
spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into five groups with sklearn.model_selection.GroupKFold using the Murcko scaffold SMILES (from rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) as the group label, so internal validation mirrors the outer protocol. For each candidate stage-2 round count in 200, 400, 800 and 1600, compute the mean out-of-fold MAE of the full pipeline, choose the best count, then refit on all training rows with that count and predict the test set. Everything else stays as it is. This replaces a fixed guess with a per-fold choice at the cost of about five extra fits.
